analogy: an assembly line with fixed stations

A simulator answers the pilot's controls; a scripted mock replays only what was scripted, so it cannot surprise you the way a real model can.

analogy: a form at a counter with labelled boxes
breaks: A clerk reads the boxes and checks them too; a schema only describes them, so the model can still fill a box wrongly and the SDK must validate every field.

analogy: a vending machine that hands back your coin with a note
breaks: You read the note and act on it; a model may ignore an error, so the error must say exactly what to try next, and the loop still needs a cap.

analogy: passport control, where the officer reads your passport, not what you claim at the desk
breaks: A traveller carries the passport and hands it over; in an agent, your code reads the identity from the signed-in session, and the model never sees or carries the passport.
